design:
Tier 1: UI motion and agent guidance; no migration, no route or data change, no Hub-restart hazard (the guidance is a tool description and a seeded note).

Decisions (operator-approved 2026-11-14 where marked):
- Still no charting library (operator, 2026-11-14). The motion is CSS on the app's --ease and --dur-* tokens plus a little React in the existing components, so both themes and colours stay as they are.
- The motion is merged to master ahead of this document (operator, 2026-11-14, commit 5a9d179): hub/ui/src/styles/dashboards.css, PanelChart.tsx (ChartFrame tooltip, count-up drawn over the real figure), usePanelPresence.ts (new and leaving panels), DashboardsView.tsx (stagger, refreshing dim, skeleton), with the UI bundle rebuilt. The motion task is therefore tests against what is there, fixing only what they find; it does not rebuild the components.
- An agent's save already re-runs an open dashboard: the dashboard_saved event invalidates ['project', pid, 'dashboards'] (hub/ui/src/hooks/useSSE.ts), a prefix of the run's key, and the screen passes isFetching as refreshing; values-move and edit-visible ride on that.
- Agents never choose visual detail: guidance is about which kind and how to shape the query, never colours or motion.
- Guidance lives in the save tool's description (read every time the tool is offered) and the worked examples in the seeded data note (hub/hub/data_notes.py), where agents already go for the data's meaning.

Slice change-a-dashboard-by-asking has landed (CDA, 2026-11-14), so there is no remaining file overlap with it; the guidance task edits the save tool's description as that slice left it.

CURRENT  (master 5a9d179) motion present, proven by one mock drive only; agents get no chart-choice guidance
PROPOSED motion pinned by component tests and an acceptance drive; agents guided and checked by a real Haiku turn

problem: Slice first-dashboard (shipped 2026-11-13) drew its five chart kinds with SVG and CSS and no motion. The operator asked on 2026-11-14 for more finish and approved the mock; the operator then had the mock's motion merged to master as 5a9d179 (2026-11-14) ahead of this document, so the motion exists but is covered only by the slice-1 component tests and one mock drive. Separately, agents get the five kinds and the label-then-numbers rule (save_dashboard, hub/hub/mcp_server.py) but no word on which kind suits which question, or that bars draw in query order, that a long bar list stops being readable, or that column names become the legend and tooltip labels. Nothing tells an agent a panel will not draw until the operator opens it (drawing_warning runs only on the run route, hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py).

requirements.rationale: Tests, drives and screen readers read the page; a count-up must not make them read a wrong figure.
requirements.statement: On opening a dashboard, its panels appear one after another, bars grow from their start, lines trace from left to right, points appear after their line, and a number counts up to its value, all within 1.5 seconds; throughout, the number's element holds its real value, and no figure read from the page is ever a mid-animation value.

When an open dashboard's queries run again (Refresh, or an agent saving that dashboard), its charts dim while the queries run and then bars, lines and points move to their new values rather than the panel being redrawn from empty.

requirements.rationale: Shows the operator what an agent's change did without comparing before and after by eye.
requirements.statement: When the open dashboard gains a panel, that panel is marked once as new as it appears; when it loses one, that panel fades out where it was before it is gone; on first opening a dashboard no panel is marked new.

Hovering a bar segment or a line point shows a tooltip in the app's own style naming the point's label, its series and its value, and dims the other marks of that chart; leaving the mark removes both.
While a dashboard's queries first run, placeholders shaped like its panels shimmer where the panels will be, instead of a line of text.
When the system asks for reduced motion, nothing on the Dashboards screen animates: panels, charts and numbers appear at their final state at once, and the tooltip and dimming still work.

The save tool's guidance tells an agent which kind suits which question (one figure: number; a ranking or comparison: bar; parts of a whole across labels: stacked bar; change over time: line; detail rows: table), and how to shape a query to read well: order rows as they should be drawn, keep bar charts to about 15 labels by taking the top ones, put time in order for a line, and alias columns to the readable names the legend and tooltip will show.

requirements.rationale: An example that does not draw teaches the wrong thing; each is checked by running it.
requirements.statement: The data note every project's vault is seeded with carries one worked example per chart kind, each a query over that project's own data and its kind, and each example draws with no warning on a project that has tasks and runs.

Asked in plain words for a dashboard needing each of the five kinds, an agent on the project's cheapest model produces a dashboard whose every panel draws with no error and no drawing warning on first opening.

in_scope: Tests and a drive proving the motion already on master: staggered arrival, draw-in, count-up, values sliding on Refresh and on an agent's save, added panel marked once, removed panel fading, tooltip with dimming, skeleton, reduced motion
Fixing only what those tests and the drive find in the motion
Guidance in the save tool on choosing a chart kind and shaping its query
One worked, drawable example of each kind in the data note every project's vault is seeded with
non_goals: Rebuilding or redesigning the motion components (merged as 5a9d179)
A charting library, or new chart kinds, axes, zoom or brushing
Agents choosing colours, animation or any visual detail: the app decides how every kind looks
Changing what a query can read, or the five chart kinds
Editing dashboards in place, undo and the agent's run tool (slice change-a-dashboard-by-asking, landed)

summary: Dashboards get motion and finish: panels arrive one after another, charts draw in, a refresh or an agent's change moves values instead of redrawing them, an added panel glows and a removed one fades, hovering shows a tooltip in the app's style, and a skeleton stands in while queries first run, all turned off under reduced motion. The motion is already on master (5a9d179, merged by the operator 2026-11-14); this slice proves it with tests and a drive. Agents are also told which chart kind suits which question and how to shape a query so it reads well, with a worked example of each kind, so a dashboard asked for in plain words draws correctly the first time.

tasks.description: ac-first-time-right fails on real Haiku turns. Two ways it misses: (a) 'send-backs per model by reason' is saved as a long-format table (model, reason, count) instead of a stacked_bar, so the dashboard has four kinds; (b) the turn ends without ever calling save_dashboard: it prints the panels JSON and stops ('Let me invoke the save_dashboard tool with these panels. I need to make the actual function call now:' then exit 0), or offers 'a different approach to save this dashboard'. Rework the agent-facing guidance (save_dashboard's description in hub/hub/mcp_server.py and the stacked_bar worked example in hub/hub/data_notes.py EXAMPLES) so that a breakdown by two labels is plainly a stacked_bar whose query pivots one column per series, and so an agent saves by calling the tool rather than describing the call. Also make scripts/drive/dashboards_motion_drive.py keep the whole reply (or the save_dashboard tool result) for a turn that saves nothing, so a miss can be diagnosed. Done when the full drive passes ac-first-time-right 3 of 3 turns, on two consecutive full runs.
